# Authoring a VibeField plugin

A plugin is a directory with a manifest, one built entry module, and nothing else
the host has to be told about. The manifest is the contract: it DECLARES what the
plugin contributes, and code BINDS implementations to those declarations at
activation. Anything a plugin can do, it declares first.

These files are generated from the contracts themselves, so they describe the
schema this app actually enforces (contracts 0.1.0).

## The files

| file | what it answers |
| --- | --- |
| `manifest.md` | every manifest field, its rules, and the cross-field invariants |
| `contributions.md` | each contribution kind's shape, with a worked example |
| `widgets.md` | props, conflict groups, ports, and how a widget binds |
| `context.md` | `activate(ctx)`, which faces exist when, and the lifecycle |
| `cli.md` | the build → check → pack → dev-link loop |
| `refusals.md` | every refusal code the kit can emit, and what fixes it |

## The shortest real plugin

Three files you write, two the tools produce.

```
my-plugin/
  src/manifest.ts           # TS authors the manifest
  src/renderer.tsx          # the entry source: activate + the component
  scripts/emit-manifest.ts  # writes the canonical JSON
  vibefield.plugin.json     # EMITTED — never hand-edited
  dist/renderer.js          # BUILT — the artifact the manifest names
  package.json              # build + gen:manifest scripts
```

The manifest, complete and minimal:

```json
{
  "manifestVersion": 1,
  "id": "com.example.notes",
  "version": "0.1.0",
  "title": "Example Notes",
  "description": "A renderer-only note widget — the minimal real plugin",
  "engines": {
    "app": "^0.1.0",
    "contracts": "^0.1.0"
  },
  "entries": {
    "renderer": "./dist/renderer.js"
  },
  "activation": [
    "onWidget:com.example.notes"
  ],
  "capabilities": [
    "doc.write"
  ],
  "contributes": {
    "widgets": [
      {
        "type": "com.example.notes",
        "title": "Note",
        "description": "A sticky note",
        "category": "Cards",
        "preview": {
          "kind": "color",
          "value": "#F6E7A9"
        },
        "schemaVersion": 1,
        "surface": "dom",
        "sizeMode": "fixed",
        "defaultSize": {
          "w": 260,
          "h": 180
        },
        "minSize": {
          "w": 120,
          "h": 90
        },
        "props": {
          "text": {
            "kind": "string",
            "default": "",
            "maxLength": 4000
          },
          "color": {
            "kind": "enum",
            "options": [
              "yellow",
              "blue",
              "pink"
            ],
            "default": "yellow"
          }
        },
        "groups": {
          "text": [
            "text"
          ],
          "color": [
            "color"
          ]
        }
      }
    ]
  }
}
```

*(@vibefield/contracts fixtures/plugin-manifest.valid.json)*

The renderer module it names:

```tsx
import { defineRendererPlugin } from "@vibefield/plugin-sdk";
import type { WidgetComponentProps } from "@vibefield/plugin-sdk/canvas";
import { CardShell } from "@vibefield/plugin-sdk/ui";

function NoteCard({ world, entity }: WidgetComponentProps) {
  return (
    <CardShell world={world} entity={entity}>
      <p>hello from a plugin</p>
    </CardShell>
  );
}

export default defineRendererPlugin({
  activate(ctx) {
    ctx.widgets.register({
      type: "com.example.notes",
      binding: { component: NoteCard },
    });
  },
});
```

The manifest is AUTHORED in TypeScript and EMITTED to that JSON — you never
write the JSON by hand, and `check` refuses it if you do:

```ts
// src/manifest.ts — typed against the contract, so a mistake is a type error
import type { PluginManifestV1 } from "@vibefield/contracts";

export const manifest: PluginManifestV1 = {
  manifestVersion: 1,
  id: "com.example.notes",
  version: "0.1.0",
  title: "Example Notes",
  engines: { app: "^0.1.0", contracts: "^0.1.0" },
  entries: { renderer: "./dist/renderer.js" },
  activation: ["onWidget:com.example.notes"],
  capabilities: [],
  contributes: { widgets: [/* … */] },
};
```

```ts
// scripts/emit-manifest.ts — the one writer of the canonical artifact
import { dirname, join } from "node:path";
import { fileURLToPath } from "node:url";
import { emitManifest } from "@vibefield/plugin-build";
import { manifest } from "../src/manifest";

emitManifest(
  manifest,
  join(dirname(fileURLToPath(import.meta.url)), "..", "vibefield.plugin.json"),
);
```

The package.json that wires it together — the build script is the whole build:

```json
{
  "name": "@example/plugin-notes",
  "private": true,
  "type": "module",
  "scripts": {
    "build": "plugin-build",
    "gen:manifest": "tsx scripts/emit-manifest.ts",
    "test": "vitest run"
  },
  "dependencies": {
    "@vibefield/contracts": "workspace:*",
    "@vibefield/plugin-sdk": "workspace:*"
  },
  "peerDependencies": {
    "react": "^19.0.0"
  }
}
```

And the loop:

```sh
pnpm gen:manifest                 # manifest.ts → vibefield.plugin.json
pnpm build                        # plugin-build: renderer (+ service) bundles
vibefield-plugin check .          # the whole suite, as verdicts
vibefield-plugin dev-link .       # put it where a dev session finds it
```

Do not hand-author this layout: the scaffolder emits it working. Start every
new plugin with

```sh
create-plugin --id vendor.name --title "My Plugin" --dir plugins/name
#   (in this repo: pnpm exec create-plugin …; targets under plugins/ or
#    examples/plugins/ join the workspace — run pnpm install after)
pnpm plugin check plugins/name    # a fresh scaffold is check-clean from birth
pnpm playground plugins/name      # its starter states render as verdicts
```

The scaffold ships `manifest.ts` + its emit script, one working CardShell
widget, `playground/states.ts` starter states, the manifest conformance test,
and the build preset — every file already in the shape `check` demands.

## The rules that catch people first

- **Every contributed id is owned by the plugin id.** A widget type is `<id>` or
  `<id>.<name>`; commands and surfaces are `<id>.<name>`; behaviors are
  `<id>:<name>`; custom
  capabilities are `x.<id>.<name>`.
- **Declare before you bind.** `ctx.widgets.register` throws for a type the
  manifest does not declare, and `check` refuses a declaration nothing binds.
- **The manifest is emitted, not written.** `vibefield.plugin.json` is canonical
  key-sorted JSON; its hash is the plugin's identity. Hand-edit it and `check`
  refuses with `manifest-stale`.
- **The SDK is the only door.** Plugin code imports `@vibefield/plugin-sdk`
  (plus `/ui`, `/canvas`, `/behavior`), `@vibefield/contracts` types, and
  `react`. Nothing
  else — no host packages, no Electron, no Node builtins.
- **Absent APIs are absent, never stubbed.** If a face is missing from `ctx`,
  the manifest did not ask for it. See `context.md`.
